subject.title: fix(acpx): uncouple Codex model id from reasoning effort and drop unsupported thinking config

question: Should ACPX Codex runtime reasoning changes be supported through a mapped adapter lifecycle, or explicitly rejected to users rather than silently ignored?
rationale: The patch removes an existing user-control path, and the correct long-term behavior depends on the Codex adapter's supported mutable-session contract rather than a mechanical refactor alone.

options.title: Map supported reasoning updates
options.body: Keep bare model IDs and translate runtime reasoning changes through the adapter mechanism that actually supports session updates.

options.title: Reject unsupported updates visibly
options.body: If the adapter cannot change reasoning after launch, return a clear actionable error instead of silently discarding the requested control.

options.title: Keep launch-only behavior
options.body: Accept reasoning only at session launch, but document the limitation and preserve a clear user-visible response for later updates.

recommendation.title: Map supported reasoning updates
recommendation.body: Keep bare model IDs and translate runtime reasoning changes through the adapter mechanism that actually supports session updates.

likelyOwner.reason: A history pass is needed to identify the current ACPX/Codex runtime owner before routing this contract decision.
